description: MA state legislative election data: House (160 districts) and Senate (40 districts) races. WAR (wins above replacement) is adapted from Split Ticket's published methodology, not an original metric — see https://github.com/nesanders/ma-political-analytics/blob/HEAD/docs/PLAN.md section 4 for the full definition and citations.

seats.description: One row per (chamber, district, year): the district's partisan lean and competitiveness.

columns.vintage: redistricting vintage this district geometry belongs to, e.g. '2022-present'
columns.district_name: human-readable district name, e.g. 'Fourth Middlesex District'
columns.lean_dem_share: Democratic two-party vote share on a statewide baseline race (e.g. Governor), apportioned to this district by town-area overlap. 0.5 = even; >0.5 leans Democratic.
columns.competitiveness: Safe / Likely / Lean / Tossup, by margin from lean_dem_share
columns.competitiveness_label: competitiveness + favored party, e.g. 'Safe D', 'Tossup R'
columns.is_uncontested: true if only one major party fielded a candidate in the general
columns.turnout_ratio: this race's two-party vote total divided by the district's apportioned two-party vote total on the statewide baseline race — a 'roll-off' measure, not a share of eligible voters. Can exceed 1.0. See the methodology page.
columns.total_population: 2020 Census total population, matched by district name. Null except for the current (2022-present) vintage, and null for some Senate districts the Census name-matching couldn't resolve — see the methodology page.
columns.voting_age_population: 2020 Census voting-age (18+) population. Same coverage caveats as total_population.
columns.hispanic_or_latino_population: 2020 Census Hispanic or Latino population (any race). Same coverage caveats as total_population.
columns.median_household_income: American Community Survey 5-year median household income estimate, in dollars. Null where the Census suppressed the estimate, in addition to the total_population coverage caveats.
columns.bachelors_degree_count: ACS 5-year estimate of residents 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher. Same coverage caveats as median_household_income.

results.description: One row per candidate per general-election race — the actual outcome, joined to the seat's expected lean via WAR.

columns.district_name: human-readable district name — join key to seats.district_name
columns.party: candidate's party, or null if PD43+ has no parseable party for them
columns.winner: true if this candidate won the race
columns.is_uncontested: true if this race had no opposing major-party candidate
columns.is_incumbent: true if this candidate won the immediately preceding election for this same district within the same redistricting vintage. Never true for a district's first election on record in a vintage (nothing to compare against) — not the same as confirmed false.
columns.actual_two_party_share: this candidate's share of (Democratic + Republican) votes in the race
columns.district_lean_dem_share: the district's baseline lean at the time of this race (same as seats.lean_dem_share)
columns.war: WAR v1: actual_two_party_share minus the expected share from district_lean_dem_share alone. Only defined for Democratic/Republican candidates. Positive = overperformed the baseline; negative = underperformed. Inflated for uncontested races — see is_uncontested.
columns.war_v2: WAR v2: same as war, but the expected share also adds incumbency_adjustment when is_incumbent is true. A single fitted coefficient (see the methodology page for the current value) — the average gap between incumbents' and non-incumbents' WAR v1 over every contested major-party race. Same null cases as war.
columns.incumbency_adjustment: The fitted incumbency term war_v2 subtracts from war when is_incumbent is true, 0 otherwise. Exposed separately so a query can decompose war_v2 back into war and this.

towns.description: One row per (town, chamber, district): how much of a town's land area falls in each legislative district. A town is often split across several districts.

columns.district_id: short internal district code — join key to seats.district_id
columns.district_name: human-readable district name — join key to seats.district_name
columns.pct_of_town: share of the town's land AREA (not population) in this district, 0-1. A known simplification — see the design plan.

finance.description: OCPF campaign-finance totals per candidate per year. Only candidates matched to an OCPF filer appear here — not every candidate has one (some file exempt, some just weren't matched — see the methodology page). Absence from this table isn't evidence of zero fundraising.

columns.year: calendar year of the OCPF filing period
columns.total_raised: total dollars raised that year, summed across every matched OCPF committee
columns.total_spent: total dollars spent that year, summed across every matched OCPF committee

example_queries.question: Which Senate seats are Democratic but competitive (Tossup or Lean)?
example_queries.sql: SELECT district_name, lean_dem_share, competitiveness_label FROM seats WHERE chamber = 'senate' AND party_favored = 'Democratic' AND competitiveness IN ('Tossup', 'Lean') ORDER BY lean_dem_share

example_queries.question: Who overperformed their district's lean the most in the House in 2022?
example_queries.sql: SELECT candidate_name, district_name, party, war FROM results WHERE chamber = 'house' AND year = 2022 AND war IS NOT NULL ORDER BY war DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.question: Which House races had the lowest turnout relative to the statewide baseline in 2022?
example_queries.sql: SELECT district_name, turnout_ratio FROM seats WHERE chamber = 'house' AND year = 2022 ORDER BY turnout_ratio ASC LIMIT 10

example_queries.question: How many incumbents won re-election vs. lost, in the House in 2022?
example_queries.sql: SELECT winner, COUNT(*) AS n FROM results WHERE chamber = 'house' AND year = 2022 AND is_incumbent GROUP BY winner

example_queries.question: Which districts does Worcester span?
example_queries.sql: SELECT chamber, district_name, pct_of_town FROM towns WHERE town = 'Worcester' ORDER BY chamber, pct_of_town DESC

example_queries.question: Who raised the most money among 2022 House candidates?
example_queries.sql: SELECT f.candidate_name, f.total_raised FROM finance f JOIN results r ON r.candidate_slug = f.candidate_slug AND r.year = f.year WHERE r.chamber = 'house' AND f.year = 2022 ORDER BY f.total_raised DESC LIMIT 10

example_queries.question: Do lower-income House districts lean more Democratic or Republican?
example_queries.sql: SELECT district_name, median_household_income, lean_dem_share FROM seats WHERE chamber = 'house' AND year = 2022 AND median_household_income IS NOT NULL ORDER BY median_household_income ASC LIMIT 10
